info.title: CueRCode API
info.description:
REST API for generating, customising, and downloading QR codes. The CueRCode website uses this same API, so everything you can do on the site you can do through the API.

The API supports 26 QR code types plus 11 non-QR barcode types (via `/barcode` - see the Non-QR Barcodes section below), and 6 output formats (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF), custom colours and gradients, module and finder-pattern (marker) shapes, logo overlays, decorative frames with labels, error-correction selection, sizing, and an optional quiet zone.

## Authentication

The API supports two authentication methods (either satisfies a protected endpoint):

1. **API Key** - Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Format: `cuercode_` followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. API keys are self-service: sign in and open Account > API Keys (`/account/#api-keys-section`), or call `POST /keys` directly. The full key is shown/returned exactly once at creation (or rotation) time and can never be retrieved again - store it safely.
2. **CSRF Token** - For AJAX requests made from the website, include the session CSRF token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

Protected endpoints (`/generate`, `/preview`, `/barcode`, `/barcode/preview`, `/download/{uuid}`, `/save`, `/qrcodes`, `/qrcodes/{uuid}`, `/qrcodes/{uuid}/destination`) require one of the above. Anonymous endpoints (`/bulk-generate`, `/types`, `/formats`, `/health`) require no authentication but are still rate limited. `/account/*` and `/keys*` accept the CSRF/session method only - an `X-API-Key` request is refused with `403 ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` on `/account/*` and `403 API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` on `/keys*` (two different error codes for the two different route groups); the `/auth/*` JSON routes accept a CSRF token or an API key.

## Saved-Codes Library

`POST /save` claims a previously-generated QR code (by its `uuid`) into the authenticated caller's account, subject to the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`402 SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED` at/over the cap). `GET /qrcodes` lists only the caller's own saved codes (paginated, optionally filtered by `type`). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /qrcodes/{uuid}` operate on a single saved code: ownership is re-checked on every request from the caller's authenticated identity, never from a client-supplied field. A code that is neither owned by the caller nor marked `is_public` is reported as `404` (never `403`) to avoid disclosing that a private UUID belonging to someone else exists. `DELETE` soft-deletes (frees a `saved_codes` slot; the row is retained for audit purposes). `is_public: true` (opt-in; default `false`) grants read/download access to any authenticated caller but never write access - only the owner may `PATCH`/`DELETE`.

## Self-Service API Keys & Scopes

Authenticated users (session/CSRF only - see below) can self-service manage their own API keys under `/keys`. `POST /keys` creates a key (caller-chosen `name` + an optional `scopes` array from the allowlist below) subject to the caller's plan `api_keys` cap (`402 API_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED` at/over the cap) and returns the full raw key exactly once in the response body (`data.api_key`) - it is never retrievable again, only its HMAC-SHA256 hash is stored. `GET /keys` lists only the caller's own keys (id, prefix, name, scopes, rate limits, `is_active`, `last_used_at`, `created_at`, `expires_at` - never the secret or its hash). `POST /keys/{id}/rotate` issues a new secret for a key the caller owns (returned once, exactly like create) and immediately invalidates the old one; `DELETE /keys/{id}` revokes (deactivates) a key the caller owns. Ownership is re-checked server-side on every `{id}` operation - a key that is not owned by the caller (or does not exist) is reported as `404` (never `403`, avoiding existence disclosure).

**Session-only key management:** an `X-API-Key`-authenticated request to any `/keys*` endpoint is refused with `403 API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, regardless of that key's own scopes - only a CSRF/session-authenticated caller (such as the account page on the website) may create, list, rotate or revoke keys. This stops a compromised low-scope key (for example one that only has `generate`) from creating a new key with every scope.

**Scope allowlist:** `generate`, `preview`, `download`, `bulk`, `qrcodes:read`, `qrcodes:write`, `save`. A key with no scopes granted can authenticate but cannot access any scoped endpoint. Every scoped endpoint below documents its `requiredScope` in its own description. Scope enforcement applies only to `X-API-Key` authentication - a session/CSRF-authenticated request from the website is never scope-limited (full user rights). A key missing a route's required scope gets `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, with the missing scope named in both the `message` and a `required_scope` field alongside the standard error shape.

## Rate Limiting

All endpoints, including `/health`, are rate limited by the same per-key/per-IP mechanism (no route is exempt). Rate limit headers are included on every rate-limited response:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit` - Maximum requests per minute
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining` - Remaining requests in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` - Unix epoch time (seconds) at which the window resets
- `Retry-After` - Seconds to wait before retrying (only on `429`)

## Request Body

POST request bodies must be sent with `Content-Type: application/json` (an optional charset parameter such as `; charset=utf-8` is permitted); otherwise the API responds with `415 Unsupported Media Type`. Request bodies larger than the configured maximum (256 KiB by default) are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large`. Per-field length caps also apply (type ≤ 64 chars, each input scalar ≤ 4096 chars, frame_label ≤ 120 chars) and over-long fields are rejected with `400 FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

## Response Format

By default, responses are in JSON. To receive XML instead, either:
- Set the `Accept` header to `application/xml`, or
- Add `?format=xml` to the query string.

XML responses share the same logical structure as JSON: a root `<response>` element wrapping `success`, `message`, `data`, optional `error_code`, and `timestamp`. Arrays serialise as repeated `<item>` elements. Every XML response also includes an `<?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" href="/assets/xsl/api-response.xsl"?>` processing instruction; that stylesheet file does not exist yet, so a browser opening the raw XML directly may show a stylesheet-not-found warning - this does not affect programs/scripts reading the XML, which simply ignore the instruction.

## Output Formats

Supported formats: **PNG**, **JPG/JPEG**, **GIF**, **WebP**, **SVG**, and **PDF**. SVG additionally supports gradients and the extended (SVG-only) module/marker shapes; PDF is vector-only and does not support transparency, logo overlay, or frames.

**JPEG-XL (`jxl`) is not supported:** although the underlying schema reserves a `jxl` format value and the web server advertises the `image/jxl` MIME type, JPEG-XL is not an accepted `format` value. The server's image library does not encode JPEG-XL, so requests asking for `jxl` are coerced to `png`. Use one of the six supported formats above. For a modern, well-compressed raster format, **WebP** is the recommended alternative — it is widely supported, typically smaller than PNG, and is an accepted `format` value.

## Non-QR Barcodes

`POST /barcode` and `POST /barcode/preview` generate non-QR barcode symbologies alongside the QR codes above: 8 linear/1D types (`code128`, `code39`, `ean13`, `ean8`, `upca`, `upce`, `itf`, `codabar`) and 3 matrix/2D types (`datamatrix`, `pdf417`, `aztec`). These are deliberately separate endpoints from `/generate`/`/preview` - most QR customisation (colours, module/marker patterns, logos, frames) does not apply to a barcode symbol - accepting a small, symbology-appropriate `options` object instead (`format`: svg/png only, `scale`, `height`, `show_text`, `ecc`). Strict server-side validation runs before rendering: EAN-13/EAN-8/UPC-A check digits are computed or independently verified and rejected if wrong, UPC-E is expanded to UPC-A for check-digit verification, Code39's charset and ITF's even-length-digits-only rule are enforced - an invalid `data` value is rejected with `422 GENERATION_FAILED` naming the specific problem, never silently coerced. A generated barcode is saved and is retrievable via the same `/download/{uuid}` endpoint, saved-codes library, and `GET /types` (`typeCategory: "barcode"`) as a QR code. Reuses the `generate`/`preview` scopes (not new ones). It also depends on the `barcode_generation` plan feature, which is currently enabled on every plan, so it does not restrict anyone today.

## Versioning & Deprecation Policy

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/api/v1/`). The current version is **v1** (`info.version` 1.0.0). `/api/v1/openapi.json` is the source of truth and always reflects the deployed contract.

**Additive, backwards-compatible changes** are made within v1 without a version bump: new endpoints, new optional request fields, new response fields, and new enum/catalogue values (e.g. new QR types and new error codes in the `x-error-codes` catalogue). Clients must tolerate unknown response fields and previously-unseen enum/error-code values.

**Breaking changes are never made to v1** (removing or renaming a field/endpoint, changing a field's type or meaning, or tightening validation). Any such change would ship under a new path version (`/api/v2/`) running alongside v1.

**Deprecation:** a field or endpoint slated for future removal is marked `deprecated: true` in this spec and announced with reasonable notice; deprecated features keep working for the life of v1.

post.description:
Generate a full, non-QR barcode symbology - 8 linear (1D) types (code128, code39, ean13, ean8, upca, upce, itf, codabar) and 3 matrix (2D) types (datamatrix, pdf417, aztec). The generated code is saved exactly like a QR code (same `/download/{uuid}` endpoint, same saved-codes library), returning a UUID identifier and download URL.

**Strict server-side validation** runs before any rendering: EAN-13/EAN-8/UPC-A check digits are computed (12/7/11-digit input) or independently verified and rejected if wrong (13/8/12-digit input); UPC-E is expanded to UPC-A for check-digit verification; Code39's charset (digits, uppercase letters, space, `- . $ / + %`) and ITF's even-length-digits-only requirement are enforced. An invalid `data` value for the chosen `symbology` is rejected with `422 GENERATION_FAILED` naming the specific problem (never silently coerced).

Most QR-only customisation (colours, module/marker patterns, logos, frames) does not apply here - see `BarcodeOptions` for the small, symbology-appropriate option set this endpoint accepts instead (`format`, `scale`, `height`, `show_text`, `ecc`).

Requires authentication (API key or CSRF token). requiredScope: `generate` (the same scope as `/generate` - it is not a new scope). It also depends on the `barcode_generation` plan feature, which is currently enabled on every plan (anonymous/free/pro/business), so it does not restrict anyone today.

value.message: Barcode generated successfully.

post.summary: Bulk generate QR codes (ZIP, or an Avery label-sheet PDF)
post.description:
Generate many QR codes in a single synchronous request and receive them as a ZIP archive (`application/zip`). This endpoint is anonymous-capable (no authentication required) but is rate limited and subject to the same request-body-size cap as the other POST endpoints.

Provide either an `items` array or a `csv` string. An optional request-level `customization` object supplies shared defaults that each item's own customization overrides key-by-key.

The maximum number of items per request depends on the caller's subscription plan (`bulk_batch_size` limit) — anonymous callers get the `anonymous` plan's allowance (25 by default), while an authenticated user or API key resolves their own plan's allowance instead; exceeding it returns `413` with an `upgrade_url` hint. Per-item failures do not abort the batch — each item's outcome is recorded in a `manifest.txt` file inside the ZIP, and successfully generated images are named `NNN-<type>.<ext>`.

If the server's PHP `zip` extension is not installed, the endpoint returns `501 Not Implemented`.

**Avery label-sheet PDF:** when the request-level (shared) `customization` sets `format: pdf` and `pdf_layout` to `avery_5160` or `avery_l7160`, the response is a different shape entirely — a single combined `application/pdf` Avery label-sheet document (not a ZIP) with each item tiled into successive label slots, spanning extra sheet pages as needed. Per-item `pdf_layout`/`format` overrides are ignored in this mode (every item is forced onto the same sheet layout — a mixed-layout sheet is not a coherent single PDF); a per-item failure does not abort the sheet, but it is also not left as a blank slot — the failed item is omitted and every subsequent label shifts forward one slot to fill the gap, with the failure reflected only in the `X-Bulk-Failed` response header count (this path has no per-item manifest). See the Customization `pdf_layout` field for the full enum.

**Accessible preset:** when an item's (or the shared) `customization.preset` is `accessible`, enforcement is applied per item, exactly as on `/generate` — it forces `ecc: H`, forces `quiet_zone: true`, drops any pinned `version`, and evaluates the WCAG contrast ratio of that item's `fg_color`/`bg_color`. Unlike `/generate` (which rejects a sub-3:1 ratio with a single `422 ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW`), a `/bulk-generate` item with a sub-3:1 ratio does not abort the batch or the sheet: in the ZIP pipeline it becomes a per-item manifest failure line (`[NNN] FAILED type=... reason=Accessible preset rejected: contrast ratio X:1 is below the WCAG minimum of 3:1.`); in the Avery label-sheet PDF mode that item is omitted from the sheet entirely (not left as a blank slot — subsequent labels shift forward one slot to fill the gap), contributing to `X-Bulk-Failed` (the only place this path surfaces a failure, since it has no per-item manifest), and to the existing all-failed `422 BULK_AVERY_ALL_FAILED` if every item fails. A successfully generated accessible item's ZIP manifest OK line is followed by an additional detail line, `accessible: contrast=X:1 (level)`, plus `recommended_print_size_mm=N` when that item also supplied `scan_distance_cm`.

requiredScope: `bulk` — only enforced if the caller voluntarily supplies an `X-API-Key` on this anonymous-capable endpoint; a genuinely anonymous request never reaches the scope check at all.

items_array.summary: Explicit item list with shared defaults

200.description: ZIP archive of generated QR codes (plus manifest.txt) — or, when the shared customization requests `format: pdf` with `pdf_layout: avery_5160`/`avery_l7160`, a single combined Avery label-sheet `application/pdf` document instead. See the operation description.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for download (`cuercode-bulk.zip`, or `cuercode-bulk-avery_5160.pdf`/`cuercode-bulk-avery_l7160.pdf` for the Avery-sheet response)

X-Bulk-Failed.description: Number of items that failed (see manifest.txt; on the Avery sheet a failed item is omitted, not left as a blank slot, so this header is the only place that failure is surfaced)

application/pdf.description: Returned instead of application/zip when pdf_layout is avery_5160/avery_l7160.

get.description:
Download a previously generated QR code file by its UUID. The file is returned with the correct Content-Type header and a Content-Disposition header that triggers a browser download.

Requires authentication (API key or CSRF token). requiredScope: `download` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

**Owner-or-public access rule:** an unclaimed (never `POST /save`d) code is downloadable by any authenticated caller. A claimed code that is not marked `is_public` is downloadable only by its owner. A claimed code marked `is_public: true` is downloadable by any authenticated caller. In every denial case the response is an identical `404 NOT_FOUND` (never `403`) - this is a deliberate anti-enumeration measure so a non-owner cannot distinguish "does not exist" from "exists but is private".

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the QR code, returned by the generate endpoint

404.description: QR code not found - either the UUID is unknown/soft-deleted, the file is no longer present on disk, or (see the owner-or-public rule above) the caller is not the owner of a private claimed code. All three cases return this identical shape by design.

value.message: QR code not found.

owner_mismatch.summary: Private claimed code owned by someone else (anti-enumeration: identical to not_found)

value.message: QR code not found.

file_not_found.summary: Record exists but the underlying file is no longer present on disk

value.message: This QR code's file is no longer available for download.

post.summary: Log in and establish a session
post.description: Authenticate by email + password and, on success, start a session. Every failure (wrong password, no such account, locked account, unverified/pending account, suspended account) returns the identical 401 response - none of these states are distinguishable from the outside. Failed attempts count towards an account lockout (by default 5 failed attempts, locking the account for 15 minutes - both are configurable server settings). Requires a valid CSRF token (website) or API key. Note: the session itself is established purely via a `Set-Cookie` response header - it is not returned as a field in the JSON body; subsequent same-origin requests rely on the browser resending that cookie automatically.

post.summary: Save a generated QR code to your account
post.description: Claim a previously-generated QR code (by the `uuid` returned from POST /generate) into the authenticated caller's account, or - if the caller already owns it - update its label/visibility. Enforces the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`-1` = unlimited) only for a genuinely new claim; re-saving an already-owned code never consumes a fresh slot. A code already claimed by a different user is reported as `404` (never `403`/`409` at this stage) to avoid disclosing that the UUID belongs to somebody else. Requires a valid CSRF token (website) or API key belonging to an authenticated account. requiredScope: `save` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

get.description: **Not a JSON API endpoint** - documented here for completeness only. This is the provider's own redirect back to this app after the visitor authenticates/consents (or declines). Verifies `state` (CSRF/replay defence, single-use), exchanges `code` + the PKCE `code_verifier` for tokens at the provider's token endpoint (≤10s), cryptographically verifies the `id_token` (RS256 signature check against the provider's published keys, then iss/aud/exp/iat/nonce claim validation), then applies the account-linking decision table (create a pre-verified account / log an existing linked user in / link an additional provider onto the currently authenticated account / refuse). On a genuine sign-in outcome, issues a normal CueRCode session via the same hardened path every other login uses (session ID regenerated to prevent session fixation). Responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the caller's (re-validated, same-site-only) safe post-login destination on success, or an accessible HTML error page on any failure - never a JSON body, and no internal error detail beyond a safe generic message.

type.description: The QR code type identifier (one of 26 supported types). Use the /types endpoint to retrieve the definitive active list and each type's form field schema. Maximum 64 characters.

input.description: Type-specific input data. The required fields depend on the QR code type; use /types to obtain the form schema for each type. Each scalar field is limited to 4096 characters. Examples: url -> {"url":"https://example.com"}; wifi -> {"ssid":"...","password":"...","encryption":"WPA","hidden":false}; vcard -> {"first_name":"John","last_name":"Doe",...}; geo -> {"latitude":51.5074,"longitude":-0.1278,"label":"London"}; gs1_product -> {"gtin":"09521234543213","batch":"LOT42"}.

Customization.description: Visual customisation options for the QR code. All fields are optional; defaults are applied for missing values. The same object is accepted at the request level for bulk generation (as shared defaults) and per item/row (overriding the shared defaults key-by-key). Unknown keys are ignored.

format.description: Output image format. `jpeg` is an accepted alias of `jpg`. Note: JPEG-XL (`jxl`) is not accepted on this host (see the API description); an unrecognised value falls back to `png`.

size.description: Target image size in pixels (width/height). Clamped to the 100-4000 range server-side. Ignored by /preview (always 300px).

ecc.description: Error correction level. L=7%, M=15%, Q=25%, H=30% recovery. Higher levels tolerate more damage/obstruction. The API default is M (the website defaults to H). Use H when adding a logo.

fg_color.description: Foreground (dark module) colour as a hex code (#RGB, #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA).

bg_color.description: Background (light module) colour as a hex code.

marker_color.description: Finder pattern (corner squares) colour as a hex code. Optional; defaults to the foreground colour when omitted or empty.

pattern.description: Module (pixel) shape style. Only square/round/dot are accepted; any other value is silently coerced to square by the server.

oneOf.description: Predefined logo ID from the logo library.

`upload` to use a custom logo supplied via logo_data, an `emoji:<codepoint-seq>` native emoji centre-icon (e.g. `emoji:1f600`, `emoji:1f1fa-1f1f8` - see the emoji field description below), or a logo identifier/path.

logo.description: Logo to overlay on the QR code centre. Using a logo automatically upgrades ECC to H. Set to `upload` and provide logo_data + logo_mime for a custom image. Set to `emoji:<codepoint-seq>` to use one of the ~400 curated Twemoji (CC-BY-4.0) starter-set icons - the codepoint sequence is lowercase hex, hyphen-joined (e.g. `1f4cd` for 📍 round pushpin, `1f1fa-1f1f8` for the US flag), matching each asset's filename under `/assets/img/emoji/`. Unknown/malformed emoji sequences are silently ignored (no logo overlay, QR still generates) rather than rejected - no upload or SVG screening applies since these are our own assets, not user-supplied content. On raster output (png/jpg/gif/webp), a predefined logo (integer `logo` ID) is currently left off the image unless the server has the PHP imagick extension, because PNG copies of the predefined logo library have not been generated yet - the QR code itself still generates successfully. SVG output and emoji centre-icons are not affected, since all ~400 emoji ship with PNG copies already.

logo_data.description: Base64-encoded custom logo as a data URI (e.g. `data:image/png;base64,...`). Used only when `logo` is `upload`.

logo_mime.description: MIME type of the uploaded custom logo. Used only when `logo` is `upload`. An `image/svg+xml` logo is additionally scanned server-side and rejected with 422 LOGO_SVG_REJECTED if it contains active content (e.g. <script>, event handler attributes, external references).

logo_size_pct.description: Logo size as a percentage of the QR code dimensions. Clamped server-side to 5-40 (matches the slider range on the website).

frame_style.description: Decorative frame style drawn around the QR code. Label/banner/pill styles render the frame_label text. Not applied to PDF output. Note: unlike the other enum fields in this schema, an out-of-enum value is not rejected by a dedicated allowlist at the request-parsing layer; behaviour for an unrecognised string is delegated to the frame-rendering engine.

frame_label.description: Text label for label/banner/pill frame styles (e.g. 'SCAN ME'). Maximum 120 characters (the website limits this to 30).

frame_color.description: Frame border/background colour as a hex code.

transparent.description: Whether the background should be transparent. Honoured for PNG, GIF, WebP, and SVG; ignored for JPEG and PDF.

quiet_zone.description: Whether to include the quiet zone (the white margin around the QR code) that improves scanning reliability.

version.description: Optional fixed QR code version (1-40) controlling the module grid size (modules = 4 * version + 17). When omitted, the smallest version that fits the payload at the chosen ECC level is selected automatically.

preset.description: Customisation preset. `none` (default) applies no additional rules. `accessible` enforces an accessibility-focused configuration per ISO/IEC 18004 + WCAG 2.1: forces `ecc` to `H`, forces `quiet_zone` to `true`, drops any pinned `version` so the smallest auto-fit version is used, and evaluates the WCAG contrast ratio of `fg_color`/`bg_color`. A contrast ratio below 3:1 causes the request to be rejected with HTTP 422 (error_code `ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW`); a ratio from 3:1 up to (but not including) 4.5:1 is allowed through but reported as a non-blocking warning in the response `data.metadata.contrast_warning` field. See the /generate 422 response for a worked example. On `/bulk-generate`, this same enforcement applies per item, but a sub-3:1 contrast ratio is reported via the ZIP manifest (a `[NNN] FAILED` line) or, on the Avery sheet, by omitting that item entirely (subsequent labels shift forward — it is not left as a blank slot; the failure is reflected only in the `X-Bulk-Failed` header count there), not a request-aborting 422 — see the `/bulk-generate` operation description for the exact manifest line format.

scan_distance_cm.description: Optional intended scanning distance in centimetres, used only to compute a recommended physical print size via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (recommended size ≈ scan distance / 10, with a 20mm practical floor). When supplied together with `preset: accessible`, the recommendation is returned in the response as `data.metadata.recommended_print_size_mm`. Has no effect on the generated image itself.

gradient.description: Gradient fill for the dark modules (SVG output only). Advanced feature; not available in the website's standard generator. Ignored for non-SVG formats.

pdf_layout.description: Print layout for `format: pdf`. Ignored for any other format. `standard` (default) is today's unchanged QR-only PDF, byte-for-byte. `accessible_caption` adds a large-print (>=18pt) human-readable caption plus a Grade-1 (uncontracted) Braille caption line, rendered as geometric dot patterns (not a Unicode Braille font - core PDF fonts have no Braille glyphs). `tactile` includes everything in `accessible_caption` plus a second, clearly-delineated page containing CueRCode's own tactile locator frame overlay guide (registration marks + orientation dot), meant to be reproduced via swell paper, a Braille embosser, or a UV-varnish/raised-ink pass aligned with page 1 - this is an original design, not a reproduction of any third-party patented locator. `avery_5160` (US Letter, 3x10) and `avery_l7160` (A4, 3x7) tile the code into an Avery address-label sheet; on `/generate` a single code fills exactly one label with the rest of the sheet left blank as a printable template, while `/bulk-generate` (see BulkGenerateRequest) tiles multiple items across successive labels/pages when the same `pdf_layout` is set at the request level. See the accessibility guide at `/accessibility` for print/embossing best practice.

BulkItem.description: A single QR code request inside a bulk batch.

type.description: The QR code type identifier (e.g., 'url', 'text', 'wifi'). See GenerateRequest.type for the full enum.

input.description: Type-specific input data for this item.

customization.description: Per-item customization. Overrides the request-level shared customization key-by-key.

BulkGenerateRequest.description: A bulk generation request. Provide either an 'items' array or a 'csv' string - the server rejects a body with neither present with `400 BULK_NO_INPUT` (see the `oneOf` requirement below; a body containing both is also accepted, with 'items' taking precedence over 'csv').

items.description: Explicit list of QR code requests. Mutually exclusive with 'csv'.

csv.description: CSV body whose first non-empty line is the header row. The header must contain a 'type' column and at least one input column. Columns named 'input.<field>' (or any non-reserved column) become input fields; reserved columns (format, size, ecc, fg_color, bg_color, marker_color, pattern, marker_border, marker_center, logo, logo_size_pct, frame_style, frame_label, frame_color, transparent, quiet_zone, preset, scan_distance_cm, pdf_layout) fold into that row's customization, mirroring every key the JSON 'customization' object recognises. Note: 'version' is deliberately not a reserved column - it is a bare/'input.'-style input field instead, since it also names the vCard spec-version input field ('3.0'/'4.0') consumed by the vcard type; reserving it would misroute every vCard CSV row's version into customization, where it is rejected as an invalid QR-symbol-version override. Pin the QR symbol version via the JSON 'items' shape's 'customization' object instead. The boolean columns ('transparent', 'quiet_zone') accept 'true'/'false'/'1'/'0'/'yes'/'no' case-insensitively (any other non-empty value coerces to true). Mutually exclusive with 'items'.

customization.description: Shared customization defaults applied to every item (overridden by per-item/per-row customization).

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the generated QR code. Use this with the /download endpoint.

image.description: Base64 data URI of the generated QR code image

download_url.description: Relative URL for downloading the QR code file

mime_type.description: MIME type of the generated image

image.description: Base64 data URI of the preview image (always PNG, 300px)

AccessibleMetadata.description: Present in /generate and /preview responses only when the request's customization.preset was 'accessible'. Absent entirely for preset=none (the default).

accessible.description: Always true when this object is present.

contrast_ratio.description: The WCAG contrast ratio computed between fg_color and bg_color, rounded to 2 decimal places. Range 1.0-21.0.

contrast_warning.description: Present only when 3:1 <= contrast_ratio < 4.5:1 - a non-blocking accessibility warning (requests below 3:1 are rejected with HTTP 422 instead; see the /generate 422 response).
contrast_warning.example: Contrast ratio 3.5:1 is below the recommended WCAG AA level of 4.5:1. Consider a higher-contrast colour pair for maximum readability.

recommended_print_size_mm.description: Recommended minimum print size (width = height) in millimetres, computed from the request's scan_distance_cm via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (20mm practical floor). Null when scan_distance_cm was not supplied.

BarcodeGenerateRequest.description: Request body for POST /barcode and POST /barcode/preview.

symbology.description: The barcode symbology (one of 11 supported: 8 linear/1D + 3 matrix/2D). Use GET /types (typeCategory 'barcode') to retrieve the definitive active list.

data.description: The content to encode. Strict, symbology-specific validation applies server-side (check digits for ean13/ean8/upca/upce, charset for code39/codabar, even-length-digits-only for itf, printable-ASCII for code128, valid UTF-8 up to 2048 characters for datamatrix/pdf417/aztec) - an invalid value is rejected with 422 GENERATION_FAILED naming the specific problem. See each symbology's GET /types formFieldsJSON hint for its exact rule.

BarcodeOptions.description: Rendering options for a barcode. All fields are optional; defaults are applied for missing values. Numeric fields are clamped to their documented range rather than rejected (the strict reject-on-invalid behaviour is reserved for the `data` field's check digits/charset - see BarcodeGenerateRequest). Unknown keys are ignored.

format.description: Output format. Only these two are supported for barcodes (no JPEG/GIF/WebP/PDF renderer - see GET /formats' separate `barcode_formats` list). An unrecognised value silently falls back to 'svg'.

height.description: For 1D symbologies: the absolute bar height in pixels (clamped 10-300, default 50). For 2D symbologies: a row-height multiplier (clamped 1-10, default = `scale`, giving square modules) - useful to make PDF417 rows taller for easier scanning. Absent means "use that category's own default".

show_text.description: Render the human-readable encoded value as a caption below the symbol. Applies to 1D symbologies only - a documented no-op for 2D (datamatrix/pdf417/aztec do not carry a conventional human-readable caption).

ecc.description: Error-correction hint: for `pdf417`, an ECC level 0-8 (higher = more redundancy, larger symbol); for `aztec`, an ECC percentage 1-100 (default 33). A documented no-op for every other symbology (datamatrix uses a fixed ECC200 scheme; 1D symbologies have no ECC concept).

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the generated barcode. Use this with the /download endpoint (same mechanism as a QR code).

image.description: Raw SVG markup (format=svg) or a base64 PNG data URI (format=png).

download_url.description: Relative URL for downloading the barcode file

mime_type.description: MIME type of the generated image

image.description: Raw SVG markup (previews are always SVG)

mime_type.description: MIME type (always image/svg+xml for barcode previews)

count.description: Total number of active QR code types

name.description: Type identifier (use this in the 'type' field of generate/preview requests)

icon.description: FontAwesome icon class for displaying this type in a user interface

description.description: Brief description of the QR code type
description.example: Open a website or web page

form_fields.description: Form field schema defining the input fields for this type (name, label, type, required, validation, etc.)

payload_template.description: Template showing the generated payload format, or null when the type is built by a dedicated payload builder.

description.example: PNG image (lossless compression, transparent background support)

supports_transparency.description: Whether the format supports transparent backgrounds

supports_logo.description: Whether the format supports logo overlay

supports_frame.description: Whether the format supports frame rendering

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling. Known codes include: MISSING_FIELD, FIELD_TOO_LONG, INVALID_JSON, INVALID_CUSTOMIZATION, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, GENERATION_FAILED, LOGO_SVG_REJECTED, AUTH_REQUIRED, INVALID_API_KEY, INVALID_CSRF_TOKEN, NOT_FOUND, ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, HANDLER_NOT_FOUND, UNKNOWN_HANDLER, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, FETCH_ERROR, LOOKUP_ERROR, FILE_NOT_FOUND, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, ZIP_UNAVAILABLE, BULK_NO_INPUT, BULK_PARSE_ERROR, BULK_INVALID_BODY, BULK_VALIDATION_ERROR, BULK_INVALID_ITEMS, BULK_EMPTY, BULK_INVALID_ITEM, BULK_INVALID_CSV, BULK_CSV_NO_HEADER, BULK_CSV_NO_TYPE, BULK_CSV_NO_INPUT, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_TYPE, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_INPUT, BULK_TOO_MANY_ITEMS, BULK_TEMP_FAILED, BULK_ZIP_FAILED, BULK_READ_FAILED, BULK_AVERY_ALL_FAILED, INVALID_EMAIL, WEAK_PASSWORD, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, VERIFICATION_TOKEN_INVALID, VERIFICATION_ALREADY_USED, RESET_TOKEN_INVALID, RESET_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED, CSRF_INVALID, HASH_FAILED, ACTIVATION_FAILED, RESET_FAILED, INVALID_UUID, INVALID_LABEL, NO_FIELDS, SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED, SAVE_CONFLICT, SAVE_FAILED, LIST_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, DELETE_FAILED, REGENERATION_FAILED, FILE_SAVE_FAILED, ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW, SAVE_LOCK_BUSY, INVALID_AVATAR, AVATAR_SAVE_FAILED, AVATAR_REMOVE_FAILED, INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD, INVALID_PASSWORD, INVALID_REQUEST, CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, ALREADY_ERASED, ERASE_FAILED, ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN, LOOKUP_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN, API_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED, FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE, INVALID_SCOPE, CREATE_FAILED, ROTATE_FAILED, JSON_ENCODE_ERROR, CREDIT_INVALID_REQUEST, CREDIT_PAYG_DISABLED, CREDIT_UNAVAILABLE, CREDIT_LOCK_BUSY, CREDIT_NOT_PERMITTED, CREDIT_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, CREDIT_SPEND_CAP_EXCEEDED, CREDIT_SERVICE_ERROR (the 8 CREDIT_* codes are reserved for pay-as-you-go credit consumption, which is not available yet, so no endpoint returns them today), INVALID_DESTINATION, REDIRECT_SUSPENDED (the dynamic-redirect destination-management API's own denial shapes; PATCH /qrcodes/{uuid}/destination re-validates the destination and rejects an abuse-suspended redirect). The full, exact, machine-readable set is the x-error-codes array on this schema.

password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor - 8 is a default, not a hard-coded minimum) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.

token.description: The raw token from the emailed verification link
The raw token from the emailed reset link

new_password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.
new_password.example: a new correct horse battery staple

AuthGenericResponse.description: Generic success envelope used by every account/auth endpoint below. register/request-password-reset deliberately return an identical shape regardless of whether the target account exists (to prevent user enumeration).

message.example: If this email address is available for registration, a verification link has been sent to it.

uuid.description: The UUID returned by a prior POST /generate call

label.description: Caller-supplied nickname for this saved code. Omit to leave unchanged; an explicit empty string or null clears it.

is_public.description: Opt-in: when true, this code becomes readable/downloadable by any authenticated caller, not just the owner. Defaults to false (private) for a new claim; omitted on an already-owned code leaves its current visibility unchanged.

message.example: QR code saved to your account.

QrCodeSummary.description: One saved QR code as returned by GET /qrcodes and GET /qrcodes/{uuid}. Never includes the owner's userID/email - a public code viewed by a non-owner must not disclose who owns it.

PatchQrCodeRequest.description: All fields optional, but at least one of label/is_public/customization must be present (else 400 NO_FIELDS). "customization" fields omitted from a partial update inherit the code's existing stored value.

uuid.description: The redirect resource's own UUID - distinct from the saved QR code's UUID

previous_destination_url.description: The destinationURL value immediately before the most recent PATCH (null if never changed)

is_active.description: 0 means a visitor would get 410 Gone once the public /r/{uuid} route is available (coming soon - not available yet)

PatchRedirectDestinationRequest.description: All fields optional, but at least one of destination_url/active must be present (else 400 NO_FIELDS). destination_url is re-validated on every PATCH (allowed URL schemes only; embedded credentials, private IP addresses and self-referential redirect loops are rejected; IDN normalisation).

active.description: false = owner-initiated disable; true = re-enable a redirect you disabled yourself. A redirect already suspended for abuse rejects the whole PATCH with 409 REDIRECT_SUSPENDED before this field is ever read.

AccountProfileUpdateRequest.description: At least one of display_name, avatar_base64, or remove_avatar must be supplied. avatar_base64 and remove_avatar are mutually exclusive in effect (an upload takes precedence if both are somehow sent).

avatar_base64.description: A 'data:image/{png,jpeg,gif,webp};base64,...' data URI. SVG is explicitly rejected for avatars (to prevent stored cross-site scripting).

remove_avatar.description: Set true to clear the current custom avatar.

new_password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.

id.description: The full session identifier - pass this to DELETE /account/sessions/{id} to revoke it.

masked_id.description: The same identifier, masked for display (all but the trailing 8 characters).

is_current.description: True if this row is the session making this request.

current_password.description: The caller's current password - re-verified server-side (wrong -> 401 INVALID_PASSWORD, nothing is changed). Important: an account that signed up via SSO only (no local password ever set) can never supply a matching current_password and therefore cannot self-erase through this endpoint at all - every attempt returns 401 INVALID_PASSWORD.

confirm.description: Must be the literal boolean true - anything else (absent, "true" string, 1, false) fails closed with 400 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.

message.example: Your account has been erased. You have been signed out.

erased_at.description: The UTC timestamp the anonymization transaction committed, formatted as `Y-m-d H:i:s` (space-separated, not RFC3339/ISO-8601 - unlike `AccountDataExportResponse.data.exported_at`, which is ISO-8601). e.g. '2026-07-10 19:12:58'.

has_custom_avatar.description: True if a custom avatar file is set - the file itself is fetched separately via the session-gated /account/avatar/ endpoint, never embedded here.

payload.description: The raw, already-encoded QR payload string - never the rendered image blob.

input_data.description: The original form field values behind the payload, when captured.

customization.description: The visual customisation snapshot (colours, size, ECC, frame, etc.) used at generation time.

masked_id.description: The session identifier, masked for display - the raw, replayable token is never included in an export.

masked_subject.description: The provider subject identifier, masked - never the tokensEncrypted bundle.

message.example: Your account data export is ready.

profile.description: null if the profile row could not be looked up (e.g. a transient database error during export assembly); otherwise always populated for an existing account.

name.description: A caller-chosen label to tell your keys apart (maximum 100 characters).

scopes.description: Scopes to grant this key, from the allowlist. Omitted/empty means the key is granted no scopes (it can authenticate but cannot access any scoped endpoint).

ApiKeySecretResponse.description: The one-time response shape returned by POST /keys (create) and POST /keys/{id}/rotate - `data.api_key` is the only time the full raw key is ever returned; it cannot be retrieved again afterward (only its hash is stored).

message.example: API key created. Copy it now - it will not be shown again.

id.description: The key's numeric ID - pass this to POST /keys/{id}/rotate or DELETE /keys/{id}.

api_key.description: The full raw API key. Shown only here, only once - copy it now.

prefix.description: The same key's first 12 characters, for identification in the dashboard list (this alone is not a usable credential).

scopes.description: Present on create only (rotate preserves the existing scopes without re-stating them in the response).

rate_limits.description: Present on create only. Derived from the owning user's current plan at creation time.

last_used_at.description: Present on create only - always null for a brand-new key.

expires_at.description: Present on create only. Self-service creation does not currently expose an expiry input (always null); the column is enforced server-side if ever set another way.

ApiKeyInfo.description: One item in GET /keys' list - never includes the full key or its hash.

is_active.description: false = revoked (soft-deleted). Revoked keys remain in this list for audit purposes.
